new.question: Is spending on track?
new.text:
Spending remains below plan across key activity groupings in the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample: Rs -41.61 crore for Activity Approved, Rs -51.96 crore for Costed activities and Rs -4.24 crore for WORK ONGOING activities. 

The below-plan amounts are spread across the sample rather than concentrated in one Gram Panchayat. Among approved activities, Biswamathpur records Rs -6.74 crore and Kalimela Rs -5.46 crore, while the other 18 Gram Panchayats account for Rs -29.40 crore. Among costed activities, Biswamathpur records Rs -7.23 crore and Kalimela Rs -5.90 crore, with Rs -38.84 crore across the other 18. For ongoing works, Dutimendi records Rs -56.88 lakh and Mendarajpur Rs -37.50 lakh, while the remaining 18 account for Rs -3.29 crore. 

The thematic pattern is also broad. In 9/16 blocks, Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village and Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village have the lowest spending measured against plan. Bhubaneswar, Rangeilunda and Baranga are among the exceptions, with Theme 5—Clean and Green Village and Theme 6 lowest, alongside 4 other exception blocks. At district level, Bargarh and Ganjam are lowest across 6/7 themes; for Theme 4, the lowest districts are Ganjam and Malkangiri. 

Review attention may focus on reconciling approved and costed activity records in Biswamathpur and Kalimela, ongoing-work records in Dutimendi and Mendarajpur, and the recurring thematic positions of Bargarh, Ganjam and Malkangiri, without losing sight of the substantial below-plan amounts spread across the other Gram Panchayats.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: How is Chikilli doing?
new.text:
In the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample, Chikilli has the lowest sanctioned amount across all fiscal years. It also has the lowest number of activities with technical and administrative approval in 5/6 fiscal years; 2023-2024 is the exception, with no clear pattern. Within Chikilli’s own records, however, 85.9% of its 640 planned activities—550 activities—are marked “Activity Approved”, making the approval and status records an important reconciliation point. 

The GP planned 640 activities with a total cost of Rs 5.51 crore. Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—accounts for 59.5% of planned cost, or Rs 3.27 crore, and 48.4% of activities. At the focus-area level, the plan is more dispersed: Maintenance of community system is the largest at 23.1% (Rs 1.27 crore), followed by Roads at 17.5% (Rs 96.53 lakh). 

Spending measured against plan is Rs -4.12 crore, indicating recorded spending below plan. Theme 6 accounts for 63.4% of this measure, or Rs -2.61 crore, while Maintenance of community system accounts for 23.9% (Rs -98.63 lakh) and Roads for 18.0% (Rs -74.02 lakh). Planned money on abandoned works totals Rs 46.72 lakh; Theme 6 accounts for 43.7% (Rs 20.44 lakh) and Theme 5—Clean and Green Village—for 33.8% (Rs 15.77 lakh). 

Recorded spending totals Rs 1.39 crore across 6 fiscal years, with the largest annual amounts in 2021-2022 at Rs 31.82 lakh and 2024-2025 at Rs 26.63 lakh. Spending linked to a planned activity totals Rs 1.30 crore, and the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across the six years; this change should be read as improved recording completeness unless the cashbook total also rose. General-component spending by activity status is concentrated in “WORK ONGOING”: it accounts for 93.1% (Rs 1.52 crore) of Rs 1.63 crore, while holding 10.2% of the 640 activities. These records point to three immediate review areas: approval and status reconciliation, the large recorded gap against plan—especially under Theme 6—and the linking of payments to planned activities.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: Where is money planned but not spent?
new.text:
Spending is recorded below plan across the listed Gram Panchayats; the negative figures represent spending below planned amounts. Biswamathpur records Rs -7.23 crore, Bheden Rs -5.60 crore and Boipariguda Rs -4.75 crore. Dutimendi records Rs -2.90 crore, Bandhpali Rs -1.94 crore, Mendarajpur Rs -1.88 crore, Hirlipali Rs -1.27 crore and Andhrua Rs -1.02 crore. Haldikudar and Barimunda record Rs -90.62 lakh and Rs -69.45 lakh, respectively. 

A recurring issue for reconciliation is the amount recorded as Uncategorised. It accounts for 59.0% of Hirlipali’s below-plan amount at Rs -75.10 lakh and 50.1% of Andhrua’s at Rs -51.17 lakh. Uncategorised entries also account for Rs -2.09 crore in Bheden, Rs -1.70 crore in Biswamathpur and Rs -91.35 lakh in Dutimendi. 

Sector-specific records also merit attention. In Boipariguda’s focus-area view, Rural housing accounts for 44.9% at Rs -2.13 crore and Drinking water for 26.5% at Rs -1.26 crore; Rural housing represents only 0.9% of the 647 activities. Water Sources & Structures records Rs -41.00 lakh in Dutimendi, Rs -32.65 lakh in Bandhpali and Rs -21.81 lakh in Haldikudar; in Haldikudar it represents 24.1% of the below-plan amount but 3.1% of the 582 activities. Other notable areas are Recreational Facilities at Rs -1.55 crore in Biswamathpur, Buildings at Rs -91.44 lakh in Bheden, and Buildings and Irrigation Sources at Rs -31.04 lakh and Rs -30.00 lakh in Mendarajpur.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: How is Barpali block doing?
new.text:
Barpali accounts for 48.4% of Bargarh district’s recorded spending, with Rs 2.64 crore across 1,447 activities in 2 Gram Panchayats. Activities are almost evenly divided between Bandhpali at 50.4% (729 activities) and Bhatigaon at 49.6% (718 activities). Spending is similarly distributed: Bandhpali records 53.1% (Rs 1.40 crore) and Bhatigaon 46.9% (Rs 1.24 crore). 

Planned cost is Rs 5.49 crore, with Bandhpali accounting for 61.0% (Rs 3.34 crore) and Bhatigaon 39.0% (Rs 2.14 crore). Recorded spending is Rs -2.85 crore against plan, indicating spending below plan; Bandhpali accounts for Rs -1.94 crore and Bhatigaon Rs -90.49 lakh, while Bandhpali’s ratio is 41.9%. Against sanction, spending is Rs -35.54 lakh, including Rs -24.73 lakh in Bandhpali and Rs -10.81 lakh in Bhatigaon; this comparison covers only activities with a sanction record on file, about one in six. Sanctioned amounts total Rs 2.96 crore, split between Bandhpali at Rs 1.62 crore and Bhatigaon at Rs 1.34 crore. 

Record completeness warrants attention: 1,067 activities are recorded without cost, almost evenly split between Bandhpali (539) and Bhatigaon (528). Spending linked to a planned activity totals Rs 2.55 crore, with Rs 1.34 crore in Bandhpali and Rs 1.20 crore in Bhatigaon; the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across six years. Cashbooks record Rs 3.59 crore received—Rs 1.99 crore in Bandhpali and Rs 1.61 crore in Bhatigaon—and Rs 3.28 crore paid out—Rs 1.78 crore and Rs 1.50 crore respectively. 

Work-status records show 171 ongoing activities, divided between Bhatigaon with 88 and Bandhpali with 83. There are also 40 abandoned activities: 25 in Bandhpali and 15 in Bhatigaon. Planned money attached to abandoned works totals Rs 93.72 lakh, concentrated in Bandhpali at Rs 70.66 lakh, compared with Rs 23.06 lakh in Bhatigaon. Expected beneficiaries total 15,651 people, with Bandhpali accounting for 72.7% (11,383 people) and Bhatigaon for 4,268 people. 

The largest planned themes are Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village at 32.8% (Rs 1.80 crore) and Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village at 30.8% (Rs 1.69 crore). Their recorded shortfalls against plan are Rs -1.01 crore for Theme 4 and Rs -72.83 lakh for Theme 6; Theme 4’s ratio is 44.1%. In the general-component focus-area classification, spending totals Rs 2.99 crore across 24 values; Drinking water is the largest at 28.6% (Rs 85.57 lakh), followed by Sanitation at 17.6% (Rs 52.54 lakh), while the other 22 account for Rs 1.61 crore.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: Which places are behaving differently from the rest?
new.text:
Chikilli is the clearest place-level outlier: unlike the other 19/20 Gram Panchayats, its spending against plan is unevenly spread across fund components, and its spending against sanction is unevenly spread across focus areas. These signals concern the distribution of spending, not the amount spent.

Spending against plan is otherwise broadly shared across Gram Panchayats, with an even spread recorded for 24/30, 25/30, 25/30 and 26/30 focus areas in the respective analyses. Fuel and fodder and Khadi are recurring exceptions in all four analyses, while Small-scale industries, Markets and fairs, and Administrative & Technical Support also appear among the unevenly distributed areas.

A separate output-type pattern applies in 17/20 Gram Panchayats, where Code 105 has the lowest spending against plan. Boipariguda and Karuabahal differ, with Code 103 lowest, while Haldikudar has Code 104 lowest. These four Gram Panchayats merit focused review of the relevant planning, sanction and spending records.

new.text:

Biswamathpur has the largest share at 13.9% (Rs -7.23 crore), followed by Kalimela at 11.3% (Rs -5.90 crore); the other 18 GPs together account for Rs -38.84 crore. Review attention should cover the wider set of GPs while prioritising reconciliation in Biswamathpur and Kalimela and examining the recurring district-level position of Bargarh and Ganjam, with Malkangiri included for Theme 4.
